15.1.simple: Krishna describes the world as an ancient fig tree (ashvattha) growing upside down: roots above in the Divine, branches spreading below. Understanding this tree means understanding the purpose of scripture.

15.2.simple: The tree's branches are fed by nature's three qualities, and its buds are the objects of the senses. Its lower roots of action keep binding us into the human world.

15.3.simple: We cannot see where this tree begins, ends or rests. Krishna says to cut its deep roots with the strong axe of detachment.

15.4.simple: After that, seek the goal from which there is no return, taking refuge in the original Divine source from which all activity flowed.

15.5.simple: Those free from pride and confusion, who have overcome attachment, stay rooted in the Self, and are beyond pleasure and pain, reach that eternal goal.

15.6.simple: Krishna's supreme abode needs no sun, moon or fire to light it. Those who reach it do not return. It is a light beyond all ordinary light.

15.7.simple: Every living being is an eternal fragment of Krishna. Living in nature, the soul draws to itself the five senses and the mind.

15.8.simple: When the soul leaves one body and enters another, it carries the mind and senses with it, as the wind carries fragrance from flowers.

15.9.simple: Using the ears, eyes, touch, taste, smell and mind, the soul experiences the world. The senses are its instruments, not its true identity.

15.10.simple: Confused people do not see the soul as it leaves, stays or experiences life. Those with the eye of wisdom do see it.

15.11.simple: Sincere seekers who discipline themselves see the Self within. Those who have not purified their minds miss it, even if they try.

15.12.simple: The light of the sun that lights the world, and the light in the moon and in fire, all come from Krishna. Every light is borrowed from the Divine.

15.13.simple: Krishna supports all beings with his energy through the earth, and as the moon he nourishes all plants. Life is sustained from a deeper source.

15.14.simple: As the digestive fire in living bodies, joined with the breath, Krishna digests the different kinds of food. Even ordinary bodily life is a divine gift.

15.15.simple: Krishna lives in every heart; from him come memory, knowledge and also forgetting. He is what all the Vedas aim to reveal.

15.16.simple: There are two kinds of beings: the perishable, which includes all bodies and things, and the imperishable, the unchanging self.

15.17.simple: Beyond both is the Supreme Person, the highest Self, who enters and sustains all the worlds without ever changing.

15.18.simple: Because he is beyond the perishable and higher even than the imperishable, Krishna is known in the world and scripture as the Supreme Person (Purushottama).

15.19.simple: Whoever knows Krishna as the Supreme Person, without confusion, knows everything worth knowing and loves him with their whole being.

15.20.simple: Krishna calls this the most secret teaching. Understanding it makes a person wise, and they feel that their life's purpose is fulfilled.

lessons.title: Cutting the tangled tree
lessons.teaching: Krishna pictures worldly life as an upside-down tree whose roots are in the Divine and whose branches spread through endless desires. Its buds are sense objects, and each one sprouts new wants. The axe of detachment cuts us free so we can turn toward what truly lasts.
lessons.keyIdea: Detachment is the axe that frees you from endless wanting.

apply.scenario: Your online wishlist keeps growing. Each time you buy something, you quickly find three more things you 'need', and your savings are slipping.
apply.question: What would the Gita suggest?
options: Buy everything at once so the wanting finally stops.
Sign up for more deal alerts so you at least pay less.
Feel ashamed and avoid looking at your bank account.
See how each want sprouts new ones, and calmly practice detachment by pausing before purchases.
apply.why: In 15.2 Krishna says sense objects are the tree's buds, and in 15.3 he says to cut it with the strong axe of detachment.

lessons.reflect: What desire in your life tends to sprout more desires the more you feed it?
lessons.practice: Remove one item from a wishlist or cart today and notice how it feels.

lessons.title: A spark of the divine
lessons.teaching: Krishna says every living being is an eternal fragment of himself. When the soul leaves a body, it carries the mind and senses onward, as the wind carries a flower's scent. The wise see the soul at work; it does not end when the body does.
lessons.keyIdea: You are an eternal spark, not a passing body.

apply.scenario: Your grandmother passed away last month. You keep feeling that everything she was is simply gone forever.
apply.question: What would the Gita suggest?
options: Let yourself grieve, while taking comfort that her soul is an eternal part of the Divine, and honor her love.
Push the grief down and stay busy so you don't feel it.
Decide that love isn't worth it if it always ends in loss.
Avoid all reminders of her so the pain fades faster.
apply.why: In 15.7 Krishna calls the soul his eternal fragment, and in 15.8 he says it moves on like wind carrying fragrance.

lessons.reflect: What 'fragrance' of a loved one's character do you carry with you?
lessons.practice: Do one small thing today in the spirit of someone you've lost or deeply love.

lessons.title: Every light is borrowed
lessons.teaching: Krishna says the light of the sun, moon and fire is his, and he nourishes plants, sustains bodies and even digests our food. He sits in every heart as the source of memory and knowledge. Our gifts are received, which invites gratitude rather than pride.
lessons.keyIdea: Your talents shine with light that comes from beyond you.

apply.scenario: You've just won a scholarship. Friends congratulate you, and you catch yourself thinking you did it entirely alone and others are simply less capable.
apply.question: What would the Gita suggest?
options: Enjoy the feeling; you earned it and others should work harder.
Downplay the win completely so you don't seem proud.
Celebrate with gratitude, remembering your abilities and support come from a source beyond you.
Immediately set a bigger goal so you can prove yourself again.
apply.why: In 15.12 Krishna says the light in the sun, moon and fire is his, and in 15.15 that memory and knowledge come from him.

lessons.reflect: Which of your abilities did you receive, rather than create entirely on your own?
lessons.practice: Before one meal today, pause and silently thank everything that brought it to you.

lessons.title: Knowing what is highest
lessons.teaching: Krishna describes the perishable (all changing things), the imperishable (the unchanging self), and the Supreme Person beyond both. Knowing this clearly, a person stops being scattered and loves with their whole being. Krishna calls this his most secret teaching, which makes life feel fulfilled.
lessons.keyIdea: Know what is highest, and give it your whole heart.

apply.scenario: You've tried a dozen self-help apps, podcasts and courses this year, dropping each after a week. You feel busy with growth but not actually changed.
apply.question: What would the Gita suggest?
options: Keep trying new programs until one finally clicks.
Get clear on what matters most to you, then commit to it wholeheartedly.
Give up on growth; it's all just marketing anyway.
Do all of them at once to make faster progress.
apply.why: In 15.19 Krishna says the one who knows him as the Supreme Person, free of confusion, worships with their whole being.

lessons.reflect: What, for you, is the 'highest' thing worth giving your whole heart to?
lessons.practice: Write one sentence naming what matters most to you, and keep it where you'll see it.
